abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disease, characterised by progressive skeletal and cardiac muscle degeneration and impaired regeneration. Repeated regenerative cycles contribute to muscle stem cell exhaustion, potentially driven by telomere shortening under chronic proliferative demand. Here, we tested whether transient delivery of hTERT mRNA can increase the relative telomere signal (Q-FISH) in patient-derived DMD myogenic progenitors (CD56+) and interstitial (CD56-) cells from two DMD donors, compared with one control donor. hTERT mRNA treatment increased the relative telomere signal and added 2 to 6 population doublings in DMD myogenic progenitors, whereas healthy donor cells showed no comparable benefit in proliferation. Exploratory transcriptomic analysis indicated genotype-associated differences in translation- and cell-cycle-related gene sets following hTERT treatment. Telomere elongation and improved proliferation were not accompanied by recovery of myogenic differentiation; no karyotypic abnormalities were detected under the conditions tested. By transiently increasing the proliferative output of dystrophic cells without genomic integration, this proof of concept provides a basis for further investigation of telomere-associated proliferative limits in DMD and a starting point for future regenerative approaches.
